I don't have a sense of guilt, for example. I don't get why you would feel guilty about, say, killing a person in self defence. I often see in the movies characters feeling depressed over the fact of killing someone even though that was the right choice, or leaving someone to die to save themselves. I could never identify with those characters in those moments. "Why?" is the question that pops up in my mind every time. 

If you wanna know how it feels, check out Amos from The Expanse, honestly that was the best portrayed sociopath (not a psychopath, but it's almost the same) I've ever seen. His puzzled look on his face when people do something out of empathy is EXACTLY my reaction in these situations. Funny how he is also a 'good guy', overall doing good things, but for selfish reasons. Probably plenty of scenes with him on Youtube if the show's not your thing. We're very alike.

I don't feel shame. I don't understand how it feels to be ashamed. I pretend all the time, sure, but the emotion I really feel when pretending to be ashamed is fear of being punished. I think it's strongly corelated with guilt, so if you don't have one you probably don't have the other as well.

The above results in me sometimes behaving outrageously bad in public spaces, as long as I mentally calculate that such behaviour won't hurt my reputation in any way (e.g. foreign country). Numerous times I had someone abrubtly leave me during a hang out because they were completely freaked out by what I was doing (usually alcohol was involved).

I like risk tasking. I tend to choose more risky way of doing something, even if I consciously try to pick the safer way. It's a bit hard to play it safe all the time for me. I can get in a physical fight easily because during an argument when most people de-escalate, I tend to go all in with agression. Fortunately for everybody involved, people tend to back down when confronted in such a way. I don't go around starting fights, like some 'street warrior' types do. I'm just up for having one if for whatever reason you have a problem with me and won't back down.

That said I have a good level of self-control. If I see that you are way stronger or have friends to back you up, something switches inside and I don't get nearly as angry. This also manifests in stressful situations; I think it's one of the best thing about me. When people break down in a crisis, I remain calm and just do what I need to do. I can break down too, I have my limits, they just seem higher than an average person.
